Overall, the laptop is very good — Fast, quite and has an excellent screen.
There are some issues, however:

1.	The camera is not an infrared camera and doesn’t work with Windows Hello face recognition.
2.	The fingerprint reader is terrible. It virtually never recognises my finger for logon, although it is quite happy to tell me that finger is registered when I try to re-enter it. You will spend a lot of time removing your fingerprints and reinstalling them, the reader will then work for a day or so, before you have to do it all again.

items.title: Perfect for uni work

This laptop has been a really solid choice for day-to-day use. items.title: Slim, Light and Surprisingly Powerful
items.body:
Coming from my previous laptop, the first thing that hit me with the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro was just how light and slim it is. It’s noticeably thinner than most laptops I’ve used, and it’s easy to forget it’s even in your bag. The chassis feels solid and premium despite the weight, and the minimalist aluminium design makes it feel like a proper high-end machine rather than a typical bulky work laptop. 

The display is probably my favourite part of the whole laptop. Samsung’s AMOLED screen looks fantastic. Colours are vibrant, blacks are properly deep, and everything just looks sharper and more lively compared to the IPS displays I’ve used on other machines. Whether you’re watching videos, editing photos, or just working with lots of windows open, it’s genuinely a pleasure to look at. Reviews consistently highlight the display as one of the standout features of the laptop. 

Battery life has also been a big step up for me. I’m easily getting through a full working day without worrying about finding a charger, which wasn’t always the case with my old laptop. Even with the OLED screen, it manages to last impressively long thanks to the efficient Intel Core Ultra chips. In testing it can run for well over 14 hours of typical use and even longer in lighter scenarios, which makes it ideal if you’re moving around a lot during the day. 

Overall the Galaxy Book6 Pro feels like a proper modern Windows laptop. It’s incredibly portable, the display is one of the best I’ve used on a laptop, and the battery life means you can actually rely on it throughout the day. Coming from a my old laptop, it just feels lighter, sleeker and far more enjoyable to use day to day.

items.title: The first true "no-compromise" Ultrabook.
items.body:
After debating for several months about ordering a new laptop, as soon as I saw the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro, I knew I had found the perfect match. I opted for the 16” 1TB/32GB version with the Intel Core Ultra X7 processor. I specifically chose this model after researching and realizing it is currently the only variant featuring Intel’s new Arc B390 GPU.
This GPU has certainly delivered as advertised. I can finally play demanding games on a device with a super-light, portable "Ultrabook" design. For a 16” machine, it is incredibly easy to take anywhere, and as soon as you open it, you’re welcomed by a 3K AMOLED display that honestly makes any content look significantly better.
I have been a Samsung mobile user for years, but this is my first Galaxy Book. I’d previously avoided them because I felt that while they looked incredible, they lacked the raw power of the heavier models from competitors. However, owning the Book6 Pro has completely changed my opinion on what can be achieved in such a slim form factor.
I’ve also been impressed by the new Galaxy AI features on the Windows 11 platform, such as Live Transcript and Note Assist. The clever combination of NPU power and Samsung’s software allows me to summarize long PDF documents or meeting notes in seconds—I never have to manually sift through pages of data again.
The battery life on this 32GB/1TB model remains excellent. The convenience of the rapid 65W USB-C charging is a game-changer, as I can use the same charger for my phone, tablet, and laptop. The Galaxy Book6 Pro is an impressive machine, boasting incredible screen clarity and an AI experience that feels more integrated than ever. It is by far the best-designed Galaxy Book to date and, in my opinion, the first true "no-compromise" Ultrabook.

items.title: Powerful but still portable
items.body:
The first difference I noticed was the centred logo on the back of the screen and also how thin the screen side had become. Apart from that, the overall aesthetics was very similar to my previous laptop (GalaxyBook 3), though another different that I got to notice quickly was the touchpad - it no longer moves physically but is haptic, which means you can effectively click anywhere on that big touchpad. As I don't carry a separate mouse with me, I found this to be very useful. The key travel of the keyboard was also decent for a laptop of this size.

My laptops have always been the 14" size as I bring it between work and home, as well as my various travels. It also means I use it in a variety of lighting conditions. I felt that the laptop was still light enough to not be too cumbersome (a big plus) while the screen had a very good colour expression whilst not been too reflective. This newest model now also supports touchscreen, which is useful when multi-tasking and scrolling.

The laptop is definitely quick and responsive. I don't play any games or edit videos but normally have aroun 5-60 tabs open across 2-3 browsers and I hardly turn my laptop off. Despite this, the laptop felt seamless and smooth in its operation. I also noticed it was considerably quieter than my previous laptop, so imagine it does a good job managing the heat.

In this era of AI, I also appreciated the various features making full use of AI - now you can basically to 'circle to search' as you do on your phone and also extract text from it - this was extremely useful for dealing with scanned PDF files. The shared storage function that lets you access data on the phone straight away also made my regular photo organising infinitely easier, without having to worry about cables etc.

The few issues I had was that this came without a charger - if you don't already own a 65W, you'll need to get one separately. The laptop also only comes in the boring grey colour and I would really like it in a ligher or more fun colourway.

items.title: Very poor, not as advertised, poor battery
items.body:
Firstly, all positive reviews are incentivised, so be warned. The purchased laptop is good value for money given the current RAM prices. I like the metal chassis; it's lightweight and thin, and the haptic trackpad is the best I have ever used. The keyboard is a little shallow and hard to press, and it makes my fingers hurt after only a short while, but I am sure I will get used to it. 

But this is where things go downhill quickly:

The laptop sometimes creaks, I think it's the bottom lid, but I'm not sure. When picking it up, it creaks; when putting my hands on the palm rest, it creaks. It does not fill me with confidence. This is the second one I purchased, and the first also made creaking, and even cracking, sounds when I picked it up with one hand. I asked support, and they said it was normal due to things rubbing inside… err, no, it's not! It also continued to make those sounds. It's an ultrabook, it will sometimes be moved or picked up with one hand.

The warranty is a joke. It comes with one year, but for more, you have to purchase insurance, which is bundled with an extended warranty, really just one extra year, and it costs alot. This is not acceptable. In the past, I have managed to extend the warranty on my laptops for up to four years at very reasonable prices, industry standard. If you are buying a highend portal laptop, the upto 4 years warranty is needed.

Lastly, and this is the big one: the “up to 30 hours” battery life is a complete lie, albeit a legal one. This laptop, and the one I returned, barely last seven hours on a full charge, and that is just from browsing at 80% brightness and doing nothing intensive. It's bad, really bad. If you read reviews, they get around 12 hours by putting the screen brightness way down, but to be honest, at that point you might as well get a basic laptop with a 250-nit display. My five-year-old gaming laptop with a desktop CPU could do six hours…

I also want to say that thermals are excellent with the fans rarely turning on, Wi-Fi 7 is awesome, and the display is nice but has colour shift when moving my head left and right, but it's not that much better than a top-of-the-range IPS 12-bit panel. Performance is also a bit odd: in some places it's snappy, but in others it really struggles (e.g. right-clicking on the desktop).

items.title: First buy for our kitchen reno
items.body:
Upgrading from our older‑style Samsung fridge to the Samsung 809L Family Hub has genuinely changed our day‑to‑day fridge and freezer experience. It also happens to be the first appliance we bought for our upcoming kitchen renovation, and it’s already set the tone for the modern look we’re going for.
We were comparing a few models, but we picked this one up on a special and it offered the best value by far. The Family Hub features have become part of our daily routine: music while cooking, the whiteboard planner for keeping organised, and SmartThings for controlling everything related to the fridge — or any other device you’ve already configured in SmartThings. In our case, that includes the Samsung air conditioners located around the house.
The size and layout are excellent. The drinks section is so convenient and well thought out. The freezer design makes everything easy to find and store (no more digging around a bottomless pit looking for something), and the ice maker produces and holds so much — plus we can schedule it so it doesn’t drop ice at night. It is also incredibly quiet; even with the ice maker running, it barely makes a sound.
It looks absolutely beautiful, works perfectly for our needs, and we just love it - don’t miss the old one at all.

My favorite is Beverage Centre. Having quick access to cold water and drinks is fantastic. The autofill Water Pitcher is a lifesaver, especially during hot days. It's always ready to go. No more waiting for water to fill up the glass.

With a humongous amount of space, this fridge can fit all our groceries with ease. It's just perfect for our big family (we never run out of room).

Overall, this Samsung fridge isn't just a fridge -- it's a smart, efficient, and stylish addition to our home. We couldn't be happier with it!

items.title: can the fridge truly be a hub for the family?
items.body:
The answer? Maybe! 
We received our family hub to much excitement a couple of weeks ago. Following some deconstruction by the delivery men, they were able to get the fridge in to the house - this thing is big! 
Once plugged in the hub was very easy to setup. I had the two eldest kids in tow (8 and 11yo) and they enjoyed putting together all the trays and peeling the film off the surfaces, "satisfying" was the word of the day. 
Overall, we feel this is an excellent fridge freezer but the more advanced features are not quite there yet. 
Pro
+ Spacious, comfortably allowing us to put 2 weeks of groceries for our family of 5.
+ Spotify connect is a big plus in our house as we always have music playing. Although the software could do with an update to allow you to set the default speaker to something other than the fridge.
+ The calendar is extremely useful for us to juggle appointments, business trips and everything in between. We can see this feature being very useful. 
+ Our children very much enjoy checking the weather app to see if they should be wearing shorts for school.
+ The meal planner with the option to order the ingredients is next level. More usage is needed to see if it'll be more than a novelty.

Cons
- the speakers are a bit flat, as you might expect but you'd never use this to play music, only to initiate music from another Device. 
- we couldn't figure out a way to have both our Samsung accounts connected at the same time. Limiting our ability to manage things like shopping lists for both adults. Nice update for the app perhaps? 
-the vision AI is very time consuming to get right. Frequently you're manually having to enter the food name. You're adding 20 minutes to the job of putting the weekly shop away.  We'd love software updates to improve this feature.

items.title: Best Buy

Bought this AC recently and it honestly turned out to be one of the best upgrades for my home. The design looks extremely modern and premium, and the moment it was installed, my living room started looking much more stylish.
The delivery and installation process was smooth and quick. What impressed me most was how many useful features are packed into this AC. I can either cool the entire room evenly or enjoy focused cooling right below the AC where I usually sit and relax. The 5-motion airflow feature makes the cooling feel much more natural and comfortable.

The sleep mode has been a complete game changer for me. The AC automatically balances the temperature during the night according to sleep patterns, so I no longer wake up feeling too cold or needing to adjust the settings again and again.

Cooling is fast, the features actually feel useful in daily life, and the overall experience feels premium. Definitely a great choice if you’re planning to buy a new AC for your home.

items.title: Book 6 Pro - so Stylish

It’s been just over a week since receiving my new Samsung Galaxy Book 6 Pro and it has been such an easy task to set up, copying settings, files, messages and programmes from my previous laptop.
As soon as I opened my new Book 6, I could tell that it was a quality product, a super thin lightweight body that felt very well designed and built with a fantastic smooth grey matte metallic finish.

Overall, this is a fast, stylish laptop with amazing graphics and connectivity particularly with other Samsung devices and therefore highly recommended by me.

items.title: Slim, Light and Surprisingly Powerful
items.body:
Coming from my previous laptop, the first thing that hit me with the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro was just how light and slim it is. It’s noticeably thinner than most laptops I’ve used, and it’s easy to forget it’s even in your bag. The chassis feels solid and premium despite the weight, and the minimalist aluminium design makes it feel like a proper high-end machine rather than a typical bulky work laptop. 

The display is probably my favourite part of the whole laptop. Samsung’s AMOLED screen looks fantastic. Colours are vibrant, blacks are properly deep, and everything just looks sharper and more lively compared to the IPS displays I’ve used on other machines. Whether you’re watching videos, editing photos, or just working with lots of windows open, it’s genuinely a pleasure to look at. Reviews consistently highlight the display as one of the standout features of the laptop. 

Battery life has also been a big step up for me. I’m easily getting through a full working day without worrying about finding a charger, which wasn’t always the case with my old laptop. Even with the OLED screen, it manages to last impressively long thanks to the efficient Intel Core Ultra chips. In testing it can run for well over 14 hours of typical use and even longer in lighter scenarios, which makes it ideal if you’re moving around a lot during the day. 

Overall the Galaxy Book6 Pro feels like a proper modern Windows laptop. It’s incredibly portable, the display is one of the best I’ve used on a laptop, and the battery life means you can actually rely on it throughout the day. Coming from a my old laptop, it just feels lighter, sleeker and far more enjoyable to use day to day.

items.title: The first true "no-compromise" Ultrabook.
items.body:
After debating for several months about ordering a new laptop, as soon as I saw the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro, I knew I had found the perfect match. I opted for the 16” 1TB/32GB version with the Intel Core Ultra X7 processor. I specifically chose this model after researching and realizing it is currently the only variant featuring Intel’s new Arc B390 GPU.
This GPU has certainly delivered as advertised. I can finally play demanding games on a device with a super-light, portable "Ultrabook" design. For a 16” machine, it is incredibly easy to take anywhere, and as soon as you open it, you’re welcomed by a 3K AMOLED display that honestly makes any content look significantly better.
I have been a Samsung mobile user for years, but this is my first Galaxy Book. I’d previously avoided them because I felt that while they looked incredible, they lacked the raw power of the heavier models from competitors. However, owning the Book6 Pro has completely changed my opinion on what can be achieved in such a slim form factor.
I’ve also been impressed by the new Galaxy AI features on the Windows 11 platform, such as Live Transcript and Note Assist. The clever combination of NPU power and Samsung’s software allows me to summarize long PDF documents or meeting notes in seconds—I never have to manually sift through pages of data again.
The battery life on this 32GB/1TB model remains excellent. The convenience of the rapid 65W USB-C charging is a game-changer, as I can use the same charger for my phone, tablet, and laptop. The Galaxy Book6 Pro is an impressive machine, boasting incredible screen clarity and an AI experience that feels more integrated than ever. It is by far the best-designed Galaxy Book to date and, in my opinion, the first true "no-compromise" Ultrabook.

items.title: Powerful but still portable
items.body:
The first difference I noticed was the centred logo on the back of the screen and also how thin the screen side had become. Apart from that, the overall aesthetics was very similar to my previous laptop (GalaxyBook 3), though another different that I got to notice quickly was the touchpad - it no longer moves physically but is haptic, which means you can effectively click anywhere on that big touchpad. As I don't carry a separate mouse with me, I found this to be very useful. The key travel of the keyboard was also decent for a laptop of this size.

My laptops have always been the 14" size as I bring it between work and home, as well as my various travels. It also means I use it in a variety of lighting conditions. I felt that the laptop was still light enough to not be too cumbersome (a big plus) while the screen had a very good colour expression whilst not been too reflective. This newest model now also supports touchscreen, which is useful when multi-tasking and scrolling.

The laptop is definitely quick and responsive. I don't play any games or edit videos but normally have aroun 5-60 tabs open across 2-3 browsers and I hardly turn my laptop off. Despite this, the laptop felt seamless and smooth in its operation. I also noticed it was considerably quieter than my previous laptop, so imagine it does a good job managing the heat.

In this era of AI, I also appreciated the various features making full use of AI - now you can basically to 'circle to search' as you do on your phone and also extract text from it - this was extremely useful for dealing with scanned PDF files. The shared storage function that lets you access data on the phone straight away also made my regular photo organising infinitely easier, without having to worry about cables etc.

The few issues I had was that this came without a charger - if you don't already own a 65W, you'll need to get one separately. The laptop also only comes in the boring grey colour and I would really like it in a ligher or more fun colourway.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro (16", Core Ultra X7, 32GB
items.body:
Purchased the Galaxy Book6 Pro (16", Core Ultra X7, 32GB) on 20th March 2026.

Overall, the laptop is very good — Fast, quite and has an excellent screen.
There are some issues, however:

1.	The camera is not an infrared camera and doesn’t work with Windows Hello face recognition.
2.	The fingerprint reader is terrible. It virtually never recognises my finger for logon, although it is quite happy to tell me that finger is registered when I try to re-enter it. You will spend a lot of time removing your fingerprints and reinstalling them, the reader will then work for a day or so, before you have to do it all again.
3.	The trackpad is erratic, the mouse stick and moves in a jerky manner. 

One final thing, although I new this at the time of purchase, for the price it should come with Windows Pro not Home.

items.title: Perfect for uni work
items.body:
This laptop has been a really solid choice for day-to-day use. One of the first things I noticed was how slim and lightweight it is—it’s easy to carry around whether I’m moving between rooms, heading out, or just working from different spots during the day. It feels practical rather than bulky, which makes a big difference over time.
Performance-wise, it handles everyday tasks smoothly. Browsing the internet, working on documents, and general admin-type jobs all run without any issues. It’s not trying to be anything over the top, but it does exactly what you need it to do reliably, which is what matters most for me.
The display is another highlight. It’s clear, bright, and makes everything from reading to watching content more enjoyable. Colours look good, and overall it feels comfortable to use for longer periods.
The only real downside I’ve noticed is the lack of an anti-glare screen. In brighter environments or near windows, reflections can be quite noticeable and sometimes distracting. It’s not a dealbreaker, but it’s something to be aware of depending on where you plan to use it.
Overall, it’s a dependable, well-designed laptop that suits everyday needs really well without overcomplicating things.

items.title: Very poor, not as advertised, poor battery
items.body:
Firstly, all positive reviews are incentivised, so be warned. The purchased laptop is good value for money given the current RAM prices. I like the metal chassis; it's lightweight and thin, and the haptic trackpad is the best I have ever used. The keyboard is a little shallow and hard to press, and it makes my fingers hurt after only a short while, but I am sure I will get used to it. 

But this is where things go downhill quickly:

The laptop sometimes creaks, I think it's the bottom lid, but I'm not sure. When picking it up, it creaks; when putting my hands on the palm rest, it creaks. It does not fill me with confidence. This is the second one I purchased, and the first also made creaking, and even cracking, sounds when I picked it up with one hand. I asked support, and they said it was normal due to things rubbing inside… err, no, it's not! It also continued to make those sounds. It's an ultrabook, it will sometimes be moved or picked up with one hand.

The warranty is a joke. It comes with one year, but for more, you have to purchase insurance, which is bundled with an extended warranty, really just one extra year, and it costs alot. This is not acceptable. In the past, I have managed to extend the warranty on my laptops for up to four years at very reasonable prices, industry standard. If you are buying a highend portal laptop, the upto 4 years warranty is needed.

Lastly, and this is the big one: the “up to 30 hours” battery life is a complete lie, albeit a legal one. This laptop, and the one I returned, barely last seven hours on a full charge, and that is just from browsing at 80% brightness and doing nothing intensive. It's bad, really bad. If you read reviews, they get around 12 hours by putting the screen brightness way down, but to be honest, at that point you might as well get a basic laptop with a 250-nit display. My five-year-old gaming laptop with a desktop CPU could do six hours…

I also want to say that thermals are excellent with the fans rarely turning on, Wi-Fi 7 is awesome, and the display is nice but has colour shift when moving my head left and right, but it's not that much better than a top-of-the-range IPS 12-bit panel. Performance is also a bit odd: in some places it's snappy, but in others it really struggles (e.g. right-clicking on the desktop).
